# NTRUEncrypt SVES-3 interoperability vectors: the IEEE Std 1363.1-2008 / ANSI X9.98
# parameter sets ees401ep1 ees449ep1 ees677ep1 ees1087ep2 ees541ep1 ees1171ep1 ees1087ep1
# ees1499ep1 and the EESS #1 v3.1 product-form set ees443ep1. Read by
# src/public_key/ntru_ees_core.rs (test_vectors) and checked by every per-set test module.
# Regenerate with scripts/ees_ref_vectors/generate.sh.
#
# ORIGIN=reference: produced by scripts/ees_ref_vectors/ees_ref_vectors.c driving Security
# Innovation's reference implementation of the standard (libntruencrypt 1.1.0, CC0,
# github.com/jschanck-si/NTRUEncrypt commit 3d36004274308feef0701bf9473e5b0775e1bf6f),
# used solely as a behavioural oracle. PK / SK are the key blobs from its keygen; MSG is
# 0, 1, max-1 and max octets long; ENC_RNG is every octet the oracle drew while encrypting
# (the random component b, bLen octets per attempt, repeated when the dm0 check rejected);
# CT is the packed ciphertext. The oracle decrypted every CT back to MSG.
#
# ORIGIN=crate-encrypt: this crate's ciphertexts under the reference key pair.
# ORIGIN=crate-keygen: a key pair from this crate's keygen seeded with
# CtrDrbgAes256(KEYGEN_SEED), and this crate's ciphertexts under it. Both were produced by
# the ignored test ntru_ees_core::tests::emit_crate_vector_blocks and fed to
# `ees_ref_vectors check` on 2026-09-10: the oracle decrypted every CT to MSG and accepted
# every PK and SK blob as a matching pair (72 records, 0 failures).
#
# Oracle verdict artefact, re-checkable: the pinned build's `ees_ref_vectors check`, run on
# 2026-09-15 over this file's blocks in file order, printed one `<set> len=<n> PASS` line per
# record and a final count line. Reference blocks (36 records, 0 failures): stdout SHA-256
# fe8fcb628998be7e1ddb864e104600aea8e96545d98a3038bfd4a5e443017814. Crate blocks, both
# ORIGIN=crate-encrypt and ORIGIN=crate-keygen (72 records, 0 failures): stdout SHA-256
# c1e111be17cf4964dbb1d74902d08d1cf5e933acda23bf5ac395864da2be1e06. To re-check, extract
# the blocks of the given origins into a file and hash the check's standard output.
# Second oracle: Security Innovation's reference sources as archived by Software Heritage
# (NTRUOpenSourceProject/ntru-crypto snapshot 14e6716f, reference-code/NTRUEncrypt rev
# 76b5bd11; its seven NTRUEncrypt sources built over the 1.1.0 headers, hash and DRBG).
# It accepted all 108 records and regenerated the reference blocks byte-identically.
#
# Discrepancy record: tbuktu/libntru, commit
# 89006474f10666ac814319c795facdb429210723, describes itself as following IEEE P1363.1.
# scripts/ees_ref_vectors/libntru_crosscheck.c ran it on the 36 reference records: it
# round-trips its own ciphertexts under the converted keys (36/36) but decrypts
# 0/36 reference ciphertexts and reproduces 0/36 of them from the recorded b.
# libntru does not interoperate with the standard; these vectors follow the reference
# implementation and the specification.
